note: Steps with 'day' are spread across the reader's goal window (182 days = a 6-month goal) and scale to their own goal. Steps with 'months' are fixed from the start date. 'course' links a step to a course status; 'auto' ticks it from other progress.

steps.title: Meet your supervisor and ask for a mentor
steps.detail:
Bring this plan. Ask three questions:
- What is our local goal for my certification (most contracting support brigades say 6 months)?
- Who is my Contracting Master Gunner (KMG)?
- Who will be my mentor while I learn the job?

steps.title: Finish your new-employee requirements
steps.detail: Complete the onboarding your civilian personnel office and command require: mandatory training, timekeeping, your performance plan. Ask your supervisor which office training you need before you can work contract actions.

steps.title: Confirm your position is coded for contracting
steps.detail: Your 36-month clock, and your eligibility for the courses and the exam, depend on being in a position coded for the Contracting functional area. Ask your supervisor or your Contracting Master Gunner (KMG) to confirm the coding and your start date in your acquisition record.
steps.verify: How coding is shown differs by organization. Your KMG can confirm it.

steps.title: Set up your accounts
steps.detail:
Get these working in your first week:
- CAC, email and certificates
- AITAS (Army training applications): check that your supervisor's email is right
- Your WarU learning account
- The Army DACM Office's CAMP portal (your acquisition career record)
- Job systems your office uses: PIEE, SAM.gov, your contract writing system (ACWS or PD2) and VCE

Some system roles take weeks to approve, so request them early.
steps.verify: Your office decides which job systems and roles you need.

steps.title: Check your transcript for courses you already have
steps.detail: Look at your WarU transcript and your ATRRS record. A course from another agency, an approved equivalent provider, or (for 51Cs) your MOS training may already count. Ask your KMG about equivalency or fulfillment before you register for anything.

steps.title: Write your Individual Development Plan (IDP)
steps.detail: Put the five courses, the exam and your target dates in your IDP so your supervisor can approve your training. Army acquisition workforce members keep their IDP through the Army DACM Office's systems; Soldiers also use Army Career Tracker.
steps.verify: Your KMG will show you where your IDP lives.

steps.title: Apply for CON 1100V, and line up CON 1200V
steps.detail: Pick the earliest CON 1100V class you can attend full time. If your KMG says you may, also request a CON 1200V class that starts after CON 1100V ends. Seats fill fast.

steps.title: Ask about new-51C onboarding in your command
steps.detail: Some commands run onboarding for newly assessed 51Cs: MICC calls its program Next Generation Acquisition Professional (NGAP), and other brigades run their own, which are not published. Ask your first sergeant or senior 51C what your command offers.

steps.title: Start the lessons: Guiding Principles first
steps.detail: Spend 20 minutes a day in this guide. Start with the Guiding Principles lessons, then drill the FAR part titles in Flashcards. Guiding Principles is the biggest exam area (42 of 150 questions).

steps.title: Complete CON 1100V (Foundational Skills)
steps.detail: Four full days, virtual. Do the pre-work before day one. You need this course before CON 1200V and CON 1400V.

steps.title: Complete CON 1200V (Pre-award)
steps.detail: Nine full days, virtual. Read the Pre-Award lessons first.

steps.title: Finish the five online modules for CON 1300V
steps.detail: FAC 069 (Price Analysis), FAC 082 (Debriefings), FAC 085 (Price Reasonableness for Simplified Acquisitions), CON 0074 (Source Selection) and CON 0470 (Contract Negotiation Techniques). Save every completion certificate; the CON 1300V instructor needs them.

steps.title: Complete CON 1400V (Post-award)
steps.detail: Five full days, virtual. It only needs CON 1100V, so use it to fill a gap while you wait for a CON 1300V seat.

steps.title: Complete CON 1300V (Award)
steps.detail: Eight full days, virtual. Bring your certificates for the five online modules.

steps.title: Complete CON 7300V (Price Analysis)
steps.detail: Required since 1 October 2026, after CON 1300V. 28 hours over 7 days, with a graded simulation at the end. Brush up on Excel first.

steps.title: Finish every lesson in this guide
steps.detail: Work through every lesson and its Check yourself questions. Revisit the ones you got wrong.

steps.title: Do CON 3910 (online exam prep)
steps.detail: About 22 hours, self-paced, with practice quizzes and a practice exam. DoW strongly encourages it before your first attempt.

steps.title: Apply for CON 3990V and book a test center
steps.detail: Apply in AITAS. After approval, Pearson emails an Authorization to Test; schedule within 90 days, at a test center if you can.

steps.title: Score 75% or better on two exam simulations
steps.detail: Take the exam simulator in Practice test under real conditions: closed book, timed, no phone. Aim for 75% or better twice. If you score lower, drill your weakest area first.

steps.title: Take CON 3990V
steps.detail: 150 questions, 3 hours, 70% to pass. Record your result in Certification 101 → The exam and this step ticks itself.

steps.title: Goal: all courses and the exam done
steps.detail: This step ticks itself when all five required courses are marked done and your exam result is a pass.

steps.title: Experience check-in (3 months)
steps.detail: Go over the Experience checklist in Certification 101 with your supervisor. Plan the kinds of work you still need to do.

steps.title: Experience check-in (6 months)
steps.detail: Halfway. Make sure you have done work from every phase: pre-award, award and post-award.

steps.title: Experience check-in (9 months)
steps.detail: Close any gaps now so your supervisor can confirm a representative sample at 12 months.

steps.title: 12 months of full-time experience
steps.detail: This step ticks itself 12 months after your start date. Your supervisor still has to confirm the experience.

steps.title: Apply for your certification
steps.detail: Once the courses, the exam and 12 months of experience are done, request the certification through your component's process. In the Army that runs through the Army DACM Office (CAMP). Have your transcript, exam result and your supervisor's confirmation ready.
steps.verify: Confirm the current request process with your KMG.

steps.title: Certified by the 36-month deadline
steps.detail: The latest date the rules allow. Tick this when your certification is granted. If you might miss it, tell your supervisor early so a waiver can be requested in time.

steps.title: Earn a credential that fits your job
steps.detail: For 51Cs, the Foundational Contingency Contracting Credential (CCON 014B) is a natural next step. Installation offices often value Operational Contracting (CCON 024) or Simplified Acquisition Procedures (CCON 022).

steps.title: Start preparing for a warrant
steps.detail: Ask your supervisor about your office's warrant path and the Contracting Officer Review Board. The Board Ready app picks up where this guide ends.

steps.title: Keep current: 80 learning hours every 2 years
steps.detail: After certification, log 80 continuous learning hours every 2 years, at least 40 on contracting topics if you follow the DPCAP recommendation.
